item.title: [61★] Tailored Magic States for Algorithmic Primitives
item.author: Matthew Steinberg, ..., Chunjun Cao, Michael Perlin
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 61 ★

Authors: Matthew Steinberg, ..., Chunjun Cao, Michael Perlin

arXiv ID: 2611.28353 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Algorithmic primitives such as adders, multipliers, and Boolean logic typically contain clusters of multi-qubit non-Clifford gates, whose decomposition into TTT and CCZCCZCCZ gates adds scheduling and spacetime overhead in fault-tolerant quantum computers. Synthillation addresses this difficulty for diagonal circuits at the third level of the Clifford hierarchy by jointly synthesizing and distilling their non-Clifford content. In this work, we develop a complementary, code-theoretic approach to synthillation. We introduce CSS-T-Product (CSS-TP) codes, whose transversal single-qubit phase gates implement multi-qubit logical diagonal gates, and give analytical rules that predict these logical gates from tensor-network operations. Using quantum LEGO, we generate code families with logical actions at the third and fourth levels of the Clifford hierarchy. We classify the resulting resource states as canonical (such as TTT or CCZCCZCCZ), tensor products of canonical states, or irreducible, i.e., not reducible to a product of non-Clifford gates via Clifford operations and logical basis changes. Conversion into Encode-TTT-Decode factories built from these codes recover known synthillation resources and prepare magic states at higher levels of the Clifford hierarchy; we analyze them with a surface-code-based model for several algorithmic primitives. We demonstrate that tailored magic factories give significant latency improvements at similar or smaller occupied spacetime volume: at code distance 212121 with one factory per resource family, they reduce the latency of a GF(28)GF(28)GF(2^{8}) multiplier and a shared-addend carry-lookahead adder by up to 48%48%48\% and 38%38%38\%, respectively, and the smallest tailored factory also lowers the occupied spacetime volume. CSS-TP codes thus connect code construction to resource factories for specific algorithmic primitives.

Matthew Steinberg, ..., Chunjun Cao, Michael Perlin

item.title: [55★] Incompressible quantum information
item.author: Lasse H. Wolff, ..., Christoph Hirche, Andreas Winter
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 55 ★

Authors: Lasse H. Wolff, ..., Christoph Hirche, Andreas Winter

arXiv ID: 2611.28361 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

For a small classical system correlated with a large one, it is always possible to compress the large system down to a size only dependent on the size of the smaller one, while preserving all correlations up to a given controllable error. Here, we show that such a statement does not hold at all when the large system is quantum mechanical. More precisely, we show that there are bipartite states such that any compression of the large system, by a non-trivial relative factor, will necessarily lead to the destruction of a significant amount of correlation, measured in mutual information. Our results therefore identify a limitation of information-bottleneck approaches to quantum machine learning, showing that a small system specifying the relevant features contained in a large quantum data set does not guarantee a compact encoding of the latter that preserves the relevant correlations.

Lasse H. Wolff, ..., Christoph Hirche, Andreas Winter

item.title: [39★] Autonomous quantum machine learning via Riemannian gradient-based optimization
item.author: Kasidit Srimahajariyapong, ..., Zoë Holmes, Supanut Thanasilp
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 39 ★

Authors: Kasidit Srimahajariyapong, ..., Zoë Holmes, Supanut Thanasilp

arXiv ID: 2611.27815 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum machine learning models typically rely on repeated quantum measurements and classical optimization during training, making the quantum-to-classical information-extraction process a fundamental bottleneck for scalability. We propose a framework for autonomous self-training quantum machine learning, based on Riemannian gradient optimization, in which the optimization proceeds entirely within the quantum domain without requiring quantum measurements or classical feedback. We derive the Riemannian gradient update rules for a broad class of learning tasks and identify sufficient conditions under which the resulting training dynamics can be realized fully autonomously. Within this regime, we establish an exponential convergence guarantee, in the training iterations, for sufficiently small step sizes, and further analyze the training cost in terms of the growth of the circuit depth. Importantly, we further show that the trained model can automatically discover symmetries hidden in the training data without a prioria priori\textit{a priori} specification. For the canonical examples of quantum phase classification and unitary learning with a hidden symmetry, our numerical study indicates that learning can be achieved at low circuit depths with only a few distinct training examples. Our results thus establish autonomous quantum machine learning as a promising paradigm that removes the classical optimization loop while retaining strong theoretical guarantees and practical performances.

Kasidit Srimahajariyapong, ..., Zoë Holmes, Supanut Thanasilp

item.title: [29★] Foliated surface codes for optimal skip-gate leakage correction
item.author: Runjiang Bi, ..., Ming Li, Shruti Puri
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 29 ★

Authors: Runjiang Bi, ..., Ming Li, Shruti Puri

arXiv ID: 2611.28219 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Skip-gate leakage --- such as atom loss in neutral-atom arrays or trapped ions, or photon loss in superconducting dual-rail qubits --- takes a qubit out of its computational subspace and removes subsequent gates acting on it. If leakage is only detectable end-of-the-line at qubit measurement, error correction circuits must be designed to periodically measure all qubits, as in SWAP-based circuits and foliation. We show that the best SWAP-based surface code, although optimal against space-like skip-gate leakage errors, is suboptimal against time-like leakage errors. By optimal, we mean that the code corrects as many leakage errors as it can detect. Remarkably, we find that the foliated surface code is optimal against both space- and time-like error configurations. We support our findings with numerical simulations. Under two-qubit gate leakage with probability 0.5%, foliation suppresses time-like errors in a distance-4 rotated stability experiment by 1380(50) per two added rounds, compared to 63(1) for the best SWAP-based circuit. In memory, the two are comparable. Under an experimentally motivated neutral-atom noise model, we find that foliation outperforms SWAP-based circuits in stability for both rotated and unrotated code geometries. This holds true for a parameter sweep that takes the neutral-atom noise model from being dominated by computational errors to atom loss. Interestingly, a SWAP-based circuit for unrotated code memory performs best when computational noise dominates over loss. Our work motivates co-designing error correction circuits with logical operations: preferring foliation when time-like errors dominate and SWAP-based circuits when space-like errors dominate.

Runjiang Bi, ..., Ming Li, Shruti Puri

item.title: [20★] Reducing RSA-2048 Factoring Resources Below One Billion Toffolis via LLM-Driven Verifiable Quantum Compilation
item.author: Xiaodi Li, ..., Linghui Chen, Tao Zhang
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 20 ★

Authors: Xiaodi Li, ..., Linghui Chen, Tao Zhang

arXiv ID: 2611.31158 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Modular exponentiation dominates the logical cost of factoring 2048-bit RSA integers (RSA-2048) with Shor's algorithm. Recent approaches based on approximate residue number systems (RNS) sharply reduce the required logical qubits, yet still demand billions of Toffoli gates. Optimizing these circuits is difficult because shared ancilla qubits and measurement-based uncomputation tightly couple the arithmetic stages, while rare overflows in compressed registers occur too infrequently for random simulation to detect. Here we use large language model (LLM)-driven search to redesign the RNS pipeline across stages and build a deterministic compiler that produces a Pareto frontier of RSA-2048 circuits. We bound rare overflow probabilities analytically and verify the resulting elementary gate sequences across all constituent RNS primes on representative circuits. Relative to Gidney's 2025 baseline under matched adder accounting, our frontier cuts the minimum qubit-Toffoli product by 70.1% and lowers expected factoring Toffolis by up to 78.6% at matched accumulator precision, bringing RSA-2048 factoring below one billion Toffolis for the first time.

Xiaodi Li, ..., Linghui Chen, Tao Zhang

item.title: [18★] Local redundancies are necessary for long-lived memories in finite spatial dimensions
item.author: Chao Yin, ..., Benedikt Placke, Vedika Khemani
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 18 ★

Authors: Chao Yin, ..., Benedikt Placke, Vedika Khemani

arXiv ID: 2611.29689 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We prove a no-go theorem for exponentially long-lived thermal memories, based on the structure of redundancies among Hamiltonian terms. For local stabilizer Hamiltonians in finite spatial dimensions, the absence of local redundancies---relations in which the product of a small number of Hamiltonian terms equals the identity---is known to preclude bulk thermodynamic phase transitions. Yet glassy dynamics can still sustain long-lived memories even without a thermodynamic transition, as demonstrated by LDPC codes on non-Euclidean graphs. A longstanding question, exemplified by Haah's cubic code, is whether such a mechanism can also support passive (quantum) memory in finite-dimensional Euclidean systems. We show that this route fails for local stabilizer Hamiltonians without local redundancies: at any constant nonzero temperature, local heat-bath dynamics is fast mixing, with O(N)O(N)O(N) mixing time, where NNN is the number of qubits. We establish this by proving a strong decay of correlations property of the thermal Gibbs state. We further prove rapid mixing with O(logN)O(logN)O(\log N) mixing time under a stronger condition on induced redundancies in suitably chosen regions. This stronger result applies to several well-studied examples, including Haah's cubic code and its generalizations, as well as three-dimensional layer codes. Our work identifies redundancy structure as a key property for understanding thermal memories.

Chao Yin, ..., Benedikt Placke, Vedika Khemani

item.title: [12★] Exponential advantage in quantum observation with one extra qubit
item.author: Zhenyu Du, ..., Vlatko Vedral, Jinzhao Sun
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 12 ★

Authors: Zhenyu Du, ..., Vlatko Vedral, Jinzhao Sun

arXiv ID: 2611.30876 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

While quantum technologies promise to revolutionise how we observe the physical world, achieving substantial advantages with minimal overhead remains a central pursuit. Here, we show that augmenting a quantum machine with just one extra qubit yields an exponential advantage in probing quantum many-body dynamics. We propose an algorithm that uses this qubit to coherently interfere dynamical trajectories, simultaneously estimating exponentially many multi-time correlators with exponentially fewer evolutions than any ancilla-free scheme. Remarkably, this advantage holds even when the ancilla-free machine has unrestricted coherence time and arbitrary adaptive control, and persists even for a single correlator. We further prove that extending coherence time exponentially enhances observational power, establishing our protocol's optimality in both space and time. Finally, we numerically demonstrate our approach by predicting higher-order probe signals in a many-body system with orders-of-magnitude fewer experimental runs than previous methods. These results highlight the broad utility of our framework across quantum learning, sensing, and simulation.

Zhenyu Du, ..., Vlatko Vedral, Jinzhao Sun

item.title: [12★] Quantum conditional relative entropy and quasi-factorization
item.author: Angelo Lucia, Ángela Capel
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 12 ★

Authors: Angelo Lucia, Ángela Capel

arXiv ID: 2611.27769 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

One of the characteristic features that distinguishes quantum systems from classical ones is the inability, except for some special cases, of defining a conditional expectation map for a given quantum state, namely a map that restricts observables to a given sub-region (or more generally, a sub-algebra of observables) while preserving expectation values. Of the many consequences of this lack of conditional expectation, we consider the problem of defining the quantum conditional relative entropy, i.e., the relative entropy between two quantum states conditioned to a sub-region or sub-algebra. We discuss how, when the conditional expectation map is not defined, there are multiple, non-equivalent ways to define a quantum conditional relative entropy quantity, and we present some of their properties. Classical conditional relative entropy has played a fundamental role in many applications to spin systems, and in particular in proving logarithmic Sobolev inequalities. A key feature of conditional relative entropy that intervenes in these results is its quasi-factorization or approximate tensorization property: informally, the relative entropy is almost super-additive over weakly-dependent sub-algebras. It is then not surprising that the key to obtaining similar applications in the quantum setting, such as quantum logarithmic Sobolev inequalities in spin systems, has been to obtain approximate factorization results for the quantum conditional relative entropy, with the added complication that there is not a unique definition of conditional relative entropy to work with. We review the recent results regarding quasi-factorization of the quantum conditional relative entropy, in strong and weak forms.

Angelo Lucia, Ángela Capel

item.title: [11★] Increasing Quantum LDPC Code Distance through Explicit Extensions
item.author: Kenta Kasai
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 11 ★

Authors: Kenta Kasai

arXiv ID: 2611.28847 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We give an explicit construction of quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes without searching for candidates at each size. A fixed pair partition (PP) and fixed integer parameters determine the parity-check matrices at a specified size. Using affine permutation matrices (APMs), we construct a [[3072,772,32]][[3072,772,32]][[3072,772,32]] code with column weight 3 and check weight 8 in each of the X and Z parity-check matrices. A construction based on circulant permutation matrices (CPMs) gives [[1270,260,≥34]][[1270,260,≥34]][[1270,260,\ge34]], with column weight 4 and check weight 10. We prove that the construction yields commuting checks and verify the resulting distances using exhaustive search and logical operators. For the main construction, we conjecture the existence of a finite structural distance upper bound and distance improvement toward that bound as the size increases.

Kenta Kasai

item.title: [10★] Non-Abelian Twist Defects in Bivariate Bicycle Codes
item.author: Rui Zeng, Li-Wei Yu
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 10 ★

Authors: Rui Zeng, Li-Wei Yu

arXiv ID: 2611.28944 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Bivariate bicycle quantum low-density parity-check codes combine efficient quantum storage with a rich Abelian anyon structure, providing a compelling platform for exploring the interplay between quantum error correction and topological order. A central challenge is how to realize domain walls that host non-Abelian twist defects at their endpoints. Here we explicitly construct electric-magnetic duality walls for arbitrary bivariate bicycle codes with finite anyon content using composite, interblock, and patch checks. These checks remove the unwanted local modes while preserving charge conversion, ensuring that topologically contractible closed ribbons act trivially on encoded states. For each fixed code, check weights and interaction ranges remain bounded independently of wall length. The wall endpoints have quantum dimension 2Q/22Q/22^{Q/2}, where QQQ counts the independent generators in each electric or magnetic charge space. As an application, we illustrate measurement-only braiding for Q=3Q=3Q=3 under the correspondence between measurements and defect transport. Our construction provides a valuable basis for exploring non-Abelian defect physics and developing logical operations in quantum low-density parity-check codes with Abelian topological order in future.

Rui Zeng, Li-Wei Yu

item.title: [10★] Quantum Dobrushin comparison and locality of fermionic equilibrium states
item.author: Lennart Becker, Harman Preet Singh, Stefan Teufel
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 10 ★

Authors: Lennart Becker, Harman Preet Singh, Stefan Teufel

arXiv ID: 2611.27873 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We prove a quantum analogue of Dobrushin's comparison theorem for lattice fermions. As in the classical case, it is a tool for proving uniqueness of equilibrium states, decay of correlations, and stability of local expectations under distant perturbations. We apply it to fermions with weak many-body interactions added to a quadratic Hamiltonian, allowing pairing, spatial inhomogeneity and long-range interactions. If the quadratic Hamiltonian is gapped, there is a coupling strength below which the thermal equilibrium (KMS) state is unique at every positive temperature and its correlations decay uniformly in the temperature. Its local expectations converge to those of the unique gapped ground state exponentially fast in the inverse temperature. In the same regime, local perturbations perturb locally in a strong sense (strong LPPL): every equilibrium state of a system with a distant defect is locally close to the equilibrium state without the defect, however strong or extended the defect is. The same holds for finite-volume Gibbs states with arbitrary even boundary terms. Without a gap, uniqueness, decay of correlations and strong LPPL hold at each positive temperature for interactions below a coupling strength that depends on the temperature. At high temperature, they hold for general interactions.

Lennart Becker, Harman Preet Singh, Stefan Teufel

item.title: [9★] Proposal for a cat-cluster-state machine gun
item.author: Haoyuan Luo, Hugo P. Stackhouse, Sahand Mahmoodian
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 9 ★

Authors: Haoyuan Luo, Hugo P. Stackhouse, Sahand Mahmoodian

arXiv ID: 2611.29965 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Non-Gaussian bosonic states such as the Schrödinger cat states are essential for continuous-variable quantum-information processing. A convenient and deterministic process for generating cat states is through the use of a Rabi interaction between a single bosonic mode and a spin which facilitates a state-dependent displacement. The lack of a Rabi interaction for propagating optical photons has rendered optical cat states elusive. Here, we show that the complex nonlinear scattering dynamics of a single-mode squeezed-vacuum state interacting with a quantum emitter can be engineered to produce a Rabi interaction between a quantum emitter and a propagating photon mode while the contributions from other orthogonal modes destructively interfere. Our protocol can deterministically prepare large-scale high-fidelity squeezed cat states from squeezed-vacuum pulses and is robust to photon loss due to spontaneous emission to non-guided modes. Extending to scattering multiple input squeezed-vacuum pulses off the quantum emitter, we propose generating linear cluster state strings with logical qubits encoded as squeezed cat states, which we refer as the cat cluster state. Our interaction scheme can potentially produce strings of entangled cat states at GHz rates using semiconductor quantum dots.

Haoyuan Luo, Hugo P. Stackhouse, Sahand Mahmoodian

item.title: [8★] Quantum resources constrain function approximation
item.author: Oxana Shaya, Lirandë Pira
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 8 ★

Authors: Oxana Shaya, Lirandë Pira

arXiv ID: 2611.30789 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Universal function approximation is central to machine learning. Quantum learning models are universal as well, but this does not specify the resources needed to approximate a given function. We study how coherence, imaginarity, entanglement and magic constrain function approximation for a fixed encoding and readout, using the cumulative resource power of the trainable gates. In a one-qubit model with phase encoding, coherence bounds the oscillation of the model function, while imaginarity bounds its odd part. In a two-qubit model, entanglement bounds the distance from product functions. These bounds hold at any encoding depth. For magic, the phase encoding itself supplies non-Clifford operations. On domains bounded away from zero, Clifford trainable gates suffice for uniform approximation. Replacing unrestricted trainable gates by Clifford gates increases the encoding depth at most polynomially in the original depth, the inverse error and the inverse distance of the domain from zero. Magic in the trainable gates can nevertheless improve accuracy at fixed depth. These results show how the resources of a quantum model must match the structure of the target function.

Oxana Shaya, Lirandë Pira

item.title: [8★] Spin-adapted state preparation for quantum chemistry
item.author: Matthew L. Sims-Goh, Fredrik Hasselgren, Hamza Jnane
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 8 ★

Authors: Matthew L. Sims-Goh, Fredrik Hasselgren, Hamza Jnane

arXiv ID: 2611.30014 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum phase estimation for strongly-correlated molecules requires an initial state of high overlap with the true ground state, and preparing one is a significant fault-tolerant cost. Matrix product states (MPS) produced by the density matrix renormalisation group (DMRG) are a leading choice, yet existing circuits treat their tensors as dense or do not use the full symmetries present in molecular electronic Hamiltonians. In quantum chemistry, DMRG also exploits total spin, a non-abelian symmetry, storing one amplitude per spin multiplet instead of one per state. We show that the reduced tensors of such a spin-adapted MPS, labelled by the steps of the unitary group approach, form an abelian-symmetric MPS, which existing block-sparse preparation protocols can load at a cost set by the multiplet count. One state-independent rotation per site, determined by a Clebsch-Gordan coefficient, then returns the state to the occupation basis. We provide resource estimates for our circuits on singlet ground states of active space models of iron-sulphur clusters, finding improvements in Toffoli count up to 135×135×135\times compared to dense methods and 4.9×4.9×4.9\times compared to block-sparse methods applied to the same states, with up to 3.7×3.7×3.7\times fewer ancilla qubits required.

Matthew L. Sims-Goh, Fredrik Hasselgren, Hamza Jnane

item.title: [8★] Tackling Many-Body Coulomb Singularity by Randomization
item.author: Di Fang, Wook Yoon
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 8 ★

Authors: Di Fang, Wook Yoon

arXiv ID: 2611.27851 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Many-body Coulomb dynamics is central to quantum chemistry and molecular simulation, yet the Coulomb singularity undermines both the standard error analysis and performance of product formulas. Even for the simple hydrogen ground state, the celebrated Trotter formulas converge more slowly than their nominal order, and going to higher order does not help. Randomization by itself does not resolve this. We show that conventional qDRIFT suffers the same loss of accuracy, and that for general initial states, the errors of both Trotter formulas and qDRIFT can decrease more slowly than any power of the number of time steps (logarithmically). To overcome these limitations, we introduce supersmoothing qDRIFT, a randomized product formula that turns a physical property of free particle propagation into an algorithmic resource. Our algorithm achieves an error bound that decreases linearly with the time step, uniformly over \textitall initial states and without any smoothness or energy assumptions. Combined with spatial discretization analysis, the resulting end-to-end gate count improves on those of qubitization and high-order Trotter formulas applied directly to the discretized Hamiltonian, despite first-order convergence in time. This work demonstrates new ways of utilizing continuum dynamics to achieve algorithmic advantage.

Di Fang, Wook Yoon

item.title: [8★] Comparing weakly interacting and free quantum dynamics locally
item.author: Jorge Acuña Flores, ..., Marius Lemm, Daniele Toniolo
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 8 ★

Authors: Jorge Acuña Flores, ..., Marius Lemm, Daniele Toniolo

arXiv ID: 2611.27707 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Lieb-Robinson bounds (LRBs) have become a standard tool for perturbative results in quantum many-body physics, including gap stability and many-body adiabatic theory. Here, we use LRBs to locally approximate weakly interacting many-body dynamics with one-body dynamics on large, perturbative time scales. This allows us to use one-body transport results to establish the expected many-body transport behavior on finite time scales in the following two illustrative settings: (i) We prove quantum diffusion, as quantified by a certain operator spreading diagnostic, in weakly interacting and weakly disordered Fermi systems in dimensions D≥2D≥2D\geq2 on large finite time scales based on the non-interacting diffusion result of Black, Drogin, and Hernández [arXiv:2506.06468]. (ii) We show for Fermi-Hubbard models with initially low spin-down density, that all local multi-time spin-up correlation functions are approximated by their free counterparts. In particular, we obtain an OTOC (out-of-time-ordered correlator) counterpart to the patterns of short-time entanglement related to lattice path counts observed numerically by Bippus et al. [Phys. Rev. B 113, 035152 (2026)].

Jorge Acuña Flores, ..., Marius Lemm, Daniele Toniolo

item.title: [7★] Quantum simulation of low-temperature impurity models
item.author: Jiaqing Jiang, Nathan Ju
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 7 ★

Authors: Jiaqing Jiang, Nathan Ju

arXiv ID: 2611.30187 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum impurity models, which describe a small but strongly-interacting subsystem coupled to a large noninteracting bath, are the computational core of dynamical mean field theory and play an important role in simulating strongly correlated materials. We develop quantum algorithms for efficiently simulating these models at low temperatures and with high precision. For any impurity model on nnn fermionic modes with fixed impurity size: (1) We give a quantum algorithm that prepares the thermal state at inverse temperature ββ\beta to precision δδ\delta in time poly(n,β,log(1/δ))poly(n,β,log(1/δ))\mathrm{poly}(n,\beta,\log(1/\delta)). This algorithm is the first to achieve both polynomial scaling in the inverse temperature and polylogarithmic scaling in the precision. When the Hamiltonian has an inverse-polynomial spectral gap, our quantum algorithm prepares its ground state to precision δδ\delta in time poly(n,log(1/δ))poly(n,log(1/δ))\mathrm{poly}(n,\log(1/\delta)). (2) We further give a quantum algorithm that prepares a purification of the thermal state in time poly(n,β,log(1/δ))poly(n,β,log(1/δ))\mathrm{poly}(n,\beta,\log(1/\delta)). Using this purification, we estimate static and dynamical properties with error δδ\delta in time polynomial in nnn and ββ\beta and linear in 1/δ1/δ1/\delta up to polylogarithmic factors, achieving the Heisenberg scaling. Our algorithms build on quantum Gibbs samplers, which are quantum analogues of Markov chain Monte Carlo methods. By using global jump operators instead of local ones, we avoid the exp(β)exp(β)\exp(\beta) overhead commonly associated with quantum Gibbs samplers, making them efficient for impurity models even at low temperatures.

Jiaqing Jiang, Nathan Ju

item.title: [6★] THeatA: Transport- and Heating-aware QEC simulation with Cooling Strategies for QCCD Trapped-Ion Systems
item.author: Eitaro Ishikawa, ..., Takahiko Satoh, Shin Nishio
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 6 ★

Authors: Eitaro Ishikawa, ..., Takahiko Satoh, Shin Nishio

arXiv ID: 2611.30676 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The quantum charge-coupled device (QCCD) architecture is a promising approach to scalable trapped-ion quantum computing, enabling flexible qubit interactions by transporting ions between dedicated trap zones. Programs for such systems require operations beyond conventional circuit primitives: ion shuttling, physical SWAPs, trap splitting and merging, and cooling. Motional excitation accumulated during transport increases the mean phonon number of ions and degrades the fidelity of the two-qubit Molmer-Sorensen gates. However, existing quantum error correction (QEC) simulation frameworks do not jointly track per-ion motional excitation and explicitly schedule cooling operations with their transport time and heating costs. We develop a full-stack software framework for QEC experiments and simulations on linear QCCD systems with a single ion species, comprising an intermediate representation (IR) supporting QCCD-native operations, a compiler that translates syndrome-extraction circuits into the IR, and a heating-aware noise-injection pipeline that generates noisy Stim circuits. The compiler updates the mean phonon number of each ion throughout the schedule, and the pipeline derives gate-dependent error rates from the tracked phonon states and per-ion timing, enabling the evaluation of finite-size logical-error scaling of the rotated surface code under transport- and heating-aware noise. We show that transport-induced heating prevents logical error rates from decreasing with increasing code distance under the evaluated conditions, and that indirectly cooling the ion pairs involved in two-qubit gates, by merging them with precooled coolant ions immediately before each gate, restores this decrease. By sweeping the duration and post-cooling mean phonon number of an abstract cooling instruction, we characterize their trade-off and identify the region in which logical-error scaling is maintained.

Eitaro Ishikawa, ..., Takahiko Satoh, Shin Nishio

item.title: [5★] No-Go Theorems for Transversal and Automorphism Clifford Gates on Prime-Dimensional Qudit Stabilizer Codes
item.author: Yuchen Zhan, Qi Ye, Dong-Ling Deng
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 5 ★

Authors: Yuchen Zhan, Qi Ye, Dong-Ling Deng

arXiv ID: 2611.29430 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Logical Clifford gates are a basic primitive of fault-tolerant quantum computation. For stabilizer codes on qudits of prime dimension ppp that encode k≥2k≥2k\geq 2 logical qudits, we prove that Clifford gadgets that are transversal with respect to a fixed partition of the physical qudits into blocks of fewer than kkk qudits cannot realize the full logical Clifford group, and that this block size is tight. Code automorphisms, which combine single-qudit Clifford gates with qudit permutations, also fail for every ppp. Both obstructions come from prime-order logical Clifford elements that these gadgets cannot reach.

Yuchen Zhan, Qi Ye, Dong-Ling Deng

item.title: [4★] Simple design of adaptive protocols for quantum metrology with limited data
item.author: Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Jesús Rubio
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 4 ★

Authors: Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Jesús Rubio

arXiv ID: 2611.31230 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Recent sensing experiments have used a Bayesian notion of precision gain to adapt control parameters for fixed measurements. Here, we advocate a simple design principle based on Personick's minimum mean square loss formalism to extend this procedure in order to include measurement optimisation, determining the optimal measurement for each probe and providing a prior-dependent precision gain to optimise the probe itself. This offers a Bayesian counterpart to protocol design based on the Fisher information, with a similar algebraic structure but incorporating the full prior. We apply this principle to adaptive phase estimation with single-mode Gaussian probes, showing that joint optimisation outperforms both adaptive homodyne detection and a fixed-probe strategy optimised for the initial prior, with a maximum reduction of 32% in mean posterior variance relative to homodyne detection. Our results illustrate the potential of simple Bayesian design for quantum metrology with limited data when measurement bases can be controlled.

item.title: [4★] Quantum Cyclic XYZ Stabilizer Codes
item.author: Alessio Baldelli, ..., Davide Orsucci, Massimo Battaglioni
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 4 ★

Authors: Alessio Baldelli, ..., Davide Orsucci, Massimo Battaglioni

arXiv ID: 2611.30654 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

XYZ codes generalize the Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) framework by adding \symY\symY\sym{Y}-type stabilizers to the usual \symX\symX\sym{X}- and \symZ\symZ\sym{Z}-type ones. We study XYZ codes whose three classical component codes are binary cyclic codes of odd length~nnn. Assigning disjoint sets of irreducible factors of xn−1xn−1x^n-1 to the three Pauli types fixes the number of encoded logical qubits and ensures that the row spaces of the three parity-check matrices intersect pairwise trivially. Then, a coprimality condition between the factors assigned to each type and the reciprocals of those assigned to the others guarantees the required orthogonality. Cyclotomic cosets give a complete and explicit description of the resulting family. We show that, for odd~nnn, a cyclic stabilizer code admits an XYZ representation with cyclic component codes iff its stabilizer generators are invariant, up to a phase, under the qubit permutation i↦2imodni↦2imodni\mapsto 2i\bmod n. By fixing the length and the dimension of the code, the proposed cyclic XYZ codes attain the best known minimum distance of stabilizer codes, exceed the minimum distance of the underlying CSS codes, and even exceed the linear-programming upper bounds for general CSS codes.

item.title: [4★] Super-Multiplicativity of the Noncommutative Minimum and Applications to Quantum Privacy and Hypothesis Testing
item.author: Theshani Nuradha, ..., Mark M. Wilde, Mingze Xu
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 4 ★

Authors: Theshani Nuradha, ..., Mark M. Wilde, Mingze Xu

arXiv ID: 2611.30038 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The hockey-stick divergence is a fundamental distinguishability measure in quantum information theory. It characterizes quantum differential privacy and determines the optimal error probability of binary quantum hypothesis testing with arbitrary priors. We study how it behaves on tensor-product states. To this end, we consider the noncommutative minimum m(A,B):=(Tr[A]+Tr[B]−‖A−B‖1)/2m(A,B):=(Tr[A]+Tr[B]−∥A−B∥1)/2m(A,B):=(\mathrm{Tr}[A]+\mathrm{Tr}[B]-\|A-B\|_1)/2 of positive semidefinite operators, which reduces to ∑xmin{ax,bx}∑xmin{ax,bx}\sum_x\min\{a_x,b_x\} when AAA and BBB commute, and we prove that it is super-multiplicative, i.e., m(A⊗C,B⊗D)≥m(A,B)m(C,D)m(A⊗C,B⊗D)≥m(A,B)m(C,D)m(A\otimes C,B\otimes D)\ge m(A,B)\,m(C,D). As a consequence, we establish a sub-additivity property of the hockey-stick divergence on product states, in which the parameters of the individual systems are multiplied, and no additional prefactor appears. We show that this bound is tight, also for noncommuting states, and that it is strict for faithful states whenever at least two of the divergences are positive. Using this, we obtain sub-additivity of the Datta-Leditzky divergences, a parallel composition theorem for quantum differentially private channels under product neighboring inputs with at most linear degradation of the privacy parameters, and a sharp sub-additivity property of the hypothesis-testing relative entropy normalized by the acceptance probability. Finally, we apply the same tools to symmetric binary quantum hypothesis testing. We determine the exact prefactor of the quantum Chernoff bound for every pair of noncommuting states satisfying mild conditions including a nonlattice condition and, under a quantitative version of this condition, the full asymptotic expansion to every fixed order in 1/n1/n1/n, with explicitly computable coefficients. As a consequence, we determine the sample complexity of symmetric binary quantum hypothesis testing up to one sample, as the error probability tends to zero.

item.title: [4★] Trotter Error Bounds in Lean 4 with a Cancellation-Aware Analysis of the Fourth-Order Suzuki Formula
item.author: Bingyu Xia, Jue Xu, Yue Wang

Scites: 4 ★

Authors: Bingyu Xia, Jue Xu, Yue Wang

arXiv ID: 2611.27359 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We formalize the commutator-scaling bound of Childs et al. in Lean 4. For skew-adjoint generators, the local order condition gives an explicit integer step count sufficient to meet a prescribed error tolerance. We apply the theorem in Lean to the binary fourth-order Suzuki formula. For this formula we can also account for cancellation within and between steps. Using local remainder estimates of Casas and Murua, we sum the signed quintic and centered seventh-degree error terms after conjugating each to the interaction picture. For every positive integer step count, we bound the difference between this sum and the global error operator. At fixed time the explicit remainder is eighth order in the step size, and the integral of the conjugated quintic term gives the exact leading error coefficient. The Lean proofs cover the two-generator finite-sum estimates, including the spectral norm for complex matrices. On five ten-site nearest-neighbor Heisenberg instances at time 101010 and tolerance 10−310−310^{-3}, the transported sum meets the tolerance at a mean of 129.4129.4129.4 steps. Taking a separate norm at each step with the same polynomial and remainder gives a mean first crossing between 184.6184.6184.6 and 185.2185.2185.2 steps. The accumulated Casas--Murua local bound at q=8q=8q=8 gives a mean of 184.8184.8184.8 steps.

item.title: [3★] Froq: Safe Speculative Execution on Live Quantum States for FTQC
item.author: Yicheng Guang, Yueqi Chen
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Yicheng Guang, Yueqi Chen

arXiv ID: 2611.28427 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Reducing execution time is critical to fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) as longer executions expose logical qubits to more opportunities for failure. However, quantum processors could frequently stall due to slow classical error-correction decoders. Recent speculative decoding accelerates this process, but its speculation remains on the classical side, leaving quantum operations waiting for confirmed decoding results. Extending speculative execution to the quantum side is fundamentally challenging. Unlike classical processor states, quantum states cannot be arbitrarily copied or checkpointed for rollback, making recovery from mispredictions difficult. In this work, we propose Froq to enable safe speculative execution on live quantum states. Froq uses compiler-assisted recovery contracts to track how mispredictions propagate through quantum operations. It further employs a resource-aware runtime mechanism to reserve recovery workspace and dynamically balance the benefits of speculative execution against the expected costs of recovery. We evaluate Froq on eight FTQC programs across 88 configurations, building on an existing speculative window decoder. Froq reduces quantum-side time by 9.81% across all 88 configurations. The reduction reaches 18.34% across the 45 configurations allowing concurrent predictions, and peaks at 31.1% at code distance d=21, under limited resources.

Yicheng Guang, Yueqi Chen

item.title: [3★] Optimised 8th-Order Trotter-Suzuki Schemes for Quantum Simulation
item.author: Marko Maležič, Johann Ostmeyer
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Marko Maležič, Johann Ostmeyer

arXiv ID: 2611.27896 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Simulating quantum dynamics in many-body systems is one of the most promising applications of quantum computers. Product formulas are a natural choice for this task, since they map directly onto quantum gates, and increasing their order nnn could lead to reduced gate depths, provided the parameters are chosen efficiently. So far, schemes beyond 6th6th6^{\textrm{th}} order have only been built as compositions of second-order schemes, while more general product formulas are known only up to 6th6th6^{\textrm{th}} order. In this work, we extend our optimisation framework to order n=8n=8n = 8, and find both more efficient compositions and the first 8th8th8^{\textrm{th}} order general schemes. Our formulas improve on the theoretical efficiency of the state-of-the-art schemes by Morales et al and we recommend two schemes explicitly. In simulations of the Heisenberg XZ chain one of our recommended schemes always outperforms those by Morales et al, though it is not always the same scheme that performs best. More generally, we observe that for Hamiltonians split into many non-commuting operators the uniformity of a Trotter decomposition becomes the main indicator of a scheme's performance. To assess the schemes' use on quantum hardware, we simulate noisy circuits with our new Qiskit plugin qiskit-omelyan. At current noise levels, the Leapfrog scheme remains the best choice, but as noise rates decrease toward fault tolerance, our recommended schemes become competitive.

Marko Maležič, Johann Ostmeyer

item.title: [3★] World Models for Learning Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
item.author: Yuan Wang, Oleksandr Kyriienko
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 3 ★

Authors: Yuan Wang, Oleksandr Kyriienko

arXiv ID: 2611.27871 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We propose using world models for learning Hamiltonians from measured dynamics of a quantum computer or simulator. Implicitly, the parameters of a Hamiltonian are encoded in how the measured few-body observables evolve. By using a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) to perform prediction in latent space, we show that the device Hamiltonian can be efficiently inferred from noisy measurements. We train a spatiotemporal encoder and predictor with approximately 2.72.72.7 million trainable weights using a single objective, to predict the representation of the next window of measurements from the previous one. The network is thereby driven to retain the reproducible dynamics and discard shot noise. We recover the field and coupling maps of a two-dimensional Ising lattice in real and imaginary time, and the disorder map of a one-dimensional Heisenberg chain of 100100100 sites. In every settings the encoder achieves lower error than a masked autoencoder and than the same encoder left untrained. It also outperforms the same regression head applied directly to time-averaged observables, by factors of 4.44.44.4 to 303030. We establish latent prediction as a practical self-supervised objective for learning from measurements of quantum dynamics.

Yuan Wang, Oleksandr Kyriienko

item.title: [2★] Linear entanglement suffices for fff-routing
item.author: Kevin Bogner
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Kevin Bogner

arXiv ID: 2611.30947 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

In fff-routing, Alice receives an nnn-bit string xxx and an unknown qubit, and Bob receives an nnn-bit string yyy. They share a state prepared in advance and exchange one simultaneous message each. The party selected by the Boolean function f(x,y)f(x,y)f(x,y) must then recover the unknown qubit without further communication. To perform fff-routing successfully, Alice and Bob need to share entanglement that scales with nnn for some functions fff, but the lower and upper bounds for the entanglement are not tight. This paper shows that 2n+22n+22n+2 shared EPR pairs suffice for every function fff. The best previous bound that holds for all functions is a shared state of 2O(√nlogn)2O(nlogn√)2^{O(\sqrt{n\log n})} qubits. The new strategy moves the cost from the shared state to the messages: Alice sends an exponentially long message of 2n+1+12n+1+12^{n+1}+1 qubits, while Bob sends only classical bits. When the messages are counted towards the resources as well, the previous strategy remains the cheapest known. The result also limits lower bounds that count only the shared state: they cannot exceed a linear number of EPR pairs. The result is formalized in Lean.

Kevin Bogner

item.title: [2★] Optimal fidelity over zero-capacity erasure channels
item.author: Camilo Castro-Landolt, Rabsan Galib Ahmed, Graeme Smith
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Camilo Castro-Landolt, Rabsan Galib Ahmed, Graeme Smith

arXiv ID: 2611.30902 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Antidegradable quantum channels have zero capacity for reliable quantum communication. However, they can nevertheless transmit quantum information with nontrivial fidelity. This raises the question: how well can quantum information be preserved through such channels? In this work, we exactly characterize the optimal asymptotic entanglement fidelity of quantum erasure channels throughout the antidegradable regime. Specifically, we show that it equals γ+1−γdγ+1−γd\gamma+\frac{1-\gamma}{d} for transmission probabilities 0<γ≤120<γ≤120<\gamma\le \frac{1}{2} and logical dimension ddd. We use fractional extendibility to establish an upper bound on the entanglement fidelity achievable by arbitrary error-correcting protocols. Furthermore, we construct a family of permutation-invariant codes that asymptotically saturates this bound.

item.title: [2★] Optimizing Locally Equivalent Graph States in Quantum Computing Using Greedy Best-First Search
item.author: Sora Harada, ..., Shin Nishio, Takeaki Uno
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Sora Harada, ..., Shin Nishio, Takeaki Uno

arXiv ID: 2611.30738 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

In measurement-based quantum computation and quantum repeater networks, graph-structured quantum states called graph states play a central role as an essential resource. In a graph state, each vertex corresponds to a qubit, and each edge is prepared by applying one controlled-Z (CZ) gate. Local complementation, which toggles adjacencies among the neighbors of a selected vertex, produces operationally equivalent graph states up to an inexpensive operation called local Clifford gates. Therefore, finding equivalent graphs up to local complementation with fewer edges and lower maximum degree can reduce the preparation cost, such as the number of CZ gates and the circuit depth. In this paper, we formulate the problem of finding a desirable equivalent graph via local complementations as a state space search problem. We apply a heuristic search algorithm, greedy best-first search (GBFS), to the formulated problem. Our experimental evaluation shows that despite its simplicity, GBFS outperforms existing approaches based on integer linear programming or local search across multiple graph classes, including random graphs, bounded-degree graphs, and most of the graphs constructed from quantum LDPC codes. In addition, we empirically analyze GBFS's search behavior, confirming that we need search rather than stopping at the first local minimum to find the best solution.

Sora Harada, ..., Shin Nishio, Takeaki Uno

item.title: [2★] For whom the Bell tolls: joint measurements and state updates in quantum field theory
item.author: Christopher J. Fewster, Christiane K. M. Klein

Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Christopher J. Fewster, Christiane K. M. Klein

arXiv ID: 2611.30468 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

State update rules and their behaviour in Bell tests play an important role in the study of measurement schemes and quantum information. We consider the state updates of the Fewster-Verch measurement framework for quantum field theory using their connection to the probability distribution of measurement outcomes. We focus on a set of observables of the form A(fi)∗A(fi)A(fi)∗A(fi)A(f_i)^*A(f_i), where A(f)A(f)A(f) is the (complex) smeared field operator for any theory induced by a formally hermitian, Green hyperbolic differential operator, and where the (A(fi))i=1,…,m(A(fi))i=1,…,m(A(f_i))_{i=1, \dots, m} are assumed to be normal and mutually commuting. Under the assumption that these operators have a sufficiently nice representation on a bosonic Fock space, we derive the joint moment generating functional and the unique joint probability distribution for the observables (A(fi)∗A(fi))i=1,…,m(A(fi)∗A(fi))i=1,…,m(A(f_i)^*A(f_i))_{i=1,\dots,m}. As an application of these results, we construct a model of a Bell inequality test within quantum field theory using a recently developed coupled Proca-scalar model for polarization measurements. We show that our Bell test model can violate the CHSH inequality, approaching Tsirelson's bound for maximally entangled states in the limit where vacuum effects are perfectly rejected. These results show that the state update rules derived in the Fewster-Verch framework are compatible with strongly quantum correlations. They also support a viewpoint in which state updates should be understood in relation to available information.

Christopher J. Fewster, Christiane K. M. Klein

item.title: [2★] Extraction erases the gain: cavity loss bounds dynamical-Casimir metrology at ultrastrong coupling
item.author: Juste Deuyekbe, ..., Nsangou Mama, Serge Guy Nana Engo
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Juste Deuyekbe, ..., Nsangou Mama, Serge Guy Nana Engo

arXiv ID: 2611.29634 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Ultrastrong light--matter coupling dresses the vacuum with virtual photons whose response to the coupling strength exceeds that of any coherent probe, yet these photons never leave the cavity and cannot be detected. A parametric drive at the dynamical-Casimir resonance converts them into real photons that a detector can collect. We show that this conversion is self-limiting: converting the virtual photons of an ultrastrongly coupled probe into real, extractable photons opens the cavity port that removes them, so the retained metrological gain is set by the accumulated cavity loss rather than by the pure-state ceiling. In the driven quantum Rabi model the pure-state quantum Fisher information on the coupling reaches 1.7×1051.7×1051.7\times10^{5} times the coherent baseline; at a cavity linewidth of 246246246~MHz, typical of coplanar-waveguide flux-qubit circuits, master-equation dynamics retain 0.96%0.96%0.96\% of it. In a 32-qubit Dicke model the retained fraction is 2.6%2.6%2.6\% at the largest photon basis computed. Eighteen lossy configurations from both models fall on one curve of the accumulated loss, the product of linewidth and interrogation time, which halves the retained information at 0.130.130.13. The extraction cost, not the lossless ceiling, is the figure of merit for any protocol that reads bound vacuum correlations through a lossy port.

Juste Deuyekbe, ..., Nsangou Mama, Serge Guy Nana Engo

item.title: [2★] Quantum nonclassicality as a marginal problem
item.author: Karl Svozil
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Karl Svozil

arXiv ID: 2611.28674 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Classical explanations of quantum statistics---local, noncontextual, or causal---fail for one and the same reason: the probability distributions observed in different contexts are not the marginals of a single joint distribution. Every single context admits a classical model. This is Boole's problem of the "conditions of possible experience." Garg and Mermin treated it as a linear problem and showed, via Farkas's lemma, that its solvability is equivalent to a finite list of Bell-type inequalities, one for each extreme ray of a convex polyhedral cone; Pitowsky gave it the form of correlation polytopes. We sketch this common structure and discuss two examples: Aerts's elastic-band model, which reproduces the quantum cosine in one context but obeys the classical bound when contexts are combined; and nonclassicality in causal data fusion, where the contexts are supplied by interventions on a causal structure.

Karl Svozil

item.title: [2★] Single-realization Pauli twirling for suppressing coherent error accumulation in structured quantum circuits
item.author: Dihang Sun, ..., Nannan Ma, Jiangbin Gong
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Dihang Sun, ..., Nannan Ma, Jiangbin Gong

arXiv ID: 2611.27703 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Pauli twirling is conventionally understood as an ensemble-level noise-tailoring procedure which suppresses coherent components of the error channel by averaging over randomized compilations. This picture does not by itself determine whether a single realization of Pauli-dressed circuit can outperform its bare counterpart, nor does it predict when such an advantage should occur. In this work, we present single-realization based framework for the standard Pauli dressing of two-qubit Clifford gates in structured quantum circuits. This is afforded by the key insight that for weak coherent errors, the leading gate infidelity is governed by the variance of some accumulated error generator. Through both simulations and theoretical considerations, we verify that coherent errors accumulated at different entangling gates can produce Θ(L2)Θ(L2)\Theta(L^2) variance growth in a bare circuit, whereas independent Pauli dressing eliminates the cross-layer contribution on average and yields an O(L)O(L)O(L) variance bound at any fixed confidence level for a single randomly sampled realization. We then develop a covariance diagnostic that predicts when this mechanism is effective in error mitigation. We find a strong Pauli twirling advantage for coherent errors whose transported generators have large off-diagonal covariance, and little advantage when the covariance matrix is nearly diagonal. Hardware experiments on IBM superconducting processors demonstrate fidelity improvements for GHZ-state preparation and reduced observable errors in Trotterized transverse-field Ising dynamics. These results indicate that single realizations of Pauli twirling without ensemble averaging is a useful coherent-error suppression technique for structured circuits containing repeated nontrivial two-qubit operations.

Dihang Sun, ..., Nannan Ma, Jiangbin Gong

item.title: [2★] Emergent Causality of Macroscopic Transport and Equilibration in Long-Range Quantum Systems
item.author: Hongchao Li, Marius Lemm
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Hongchao Li, Marius Lemm

arXiv ID: 2611.27650 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Long-range couplings in quantum many-body systems challenge conventional notions of locality and causality. Here, we show that macroscopic particle transport nevertheless exhibits emergent causality --- an effective light cone that becomes strict in the thermodynamic limit. For power-law hopping with a decay exponent α∈(D,D+1)α∈(D,D+1)\alpha\in(D,D+1) in DDD spatial dimensions, the emergent causality cone expands super-ballistically, and we establish that its scaling is optimal. Our results imply lower bounds on the equilibration time of long-range systems. Finally, we construct an example of a long-range free-fermion chain with α∈(1,3/2)α∈(1,3/2)\alpha\in (1,3/2), whose macroscopic density equilibrates super-ballistically, i.e., in a time sub-linear in the system size. While long-range interactions are usually associated with slow equilibration due to increased energy barriers, our example demonstrates that long-range hopping can lead to accelerated equilibration.

Hongchao Li, Marius Lemm

item.author: Carlo Marconi
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Carlo Marconi

arXiv ID: 2611.27548 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

The quantum switch can enable communication through otherwise unusable channels, a phenomenon known as causal activation. We show that a switch of two identical pure-loss channels can achieve strictly greater energy-constrained classical and quantum capacities than their sequential use, even when two-way classical communication is available. Remarkably, the switch also activates quantum communication over a range of transmissivities for which the sequential channel has zero quantum capacity.

item.title: [2★] The inverted harmonic oscillator in Segal-Bargmann space: Time-asymmetric propagator reconstruction and bi-coherent states
item.author: Hongze Ding, Ni Liu, J.-Q. Liang
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 2 ★

Authors: Hongze Ding, Ni Liu, J.-Q. Liang

arXiv ID: 2611.27458 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We investigate the real-time dynamics and resonance quantization of the inverted harmonic oscillator (IHO). Its self-adjoint Hamiltonian on L2(R)L^2(\mathbb{R}) has a real continuous spectrum, while generalized resonance states outside L2(R)L^2(\mathbb{R}) have purely imaginary energies ±iℏω(n+1/2)\pm i\hbar\omega(n+1/2). In coordinate space, these states are expressed in terms of complex Hermite polynomials and are biorthonormal under the Fresnel Gaussian pairing. Adapting Moriconi's coordinate-time transformation to the real-time path integral, we derive the exact Feynman propagator. Using Mehler's formula, we show that each discrete expansion alone reconstructs the full unitary kernel on its time half-axis, with the decaying Gamow-Siegert branch converging for T>0T>0 and the growing antiresonant branch converging for T<0T<0. In the complex-scaled Segal-Bargmann representation, the two Hamiltonians take the form ±iℏω(z(d/dz)+1/2)\pm i\hbar\omega(z(d/dz)+1/2), and their monomial eigenfunctions map back to the dual complex Hermite states. The two convergence domains correspond to one-sided contraction semigroups of dilations. Finally, we construct bi-coherent states whose biorthogonal position and momentum second cumulants are purely imaginary and complex conjugate, with product ℏ2/4\hbar^2/4. The corresponding Heisenberg expectation values follow the exact classical hyperbolic trajectories for arbitrary real initial positions and momenta.

Hongze Ding, Ni Liu, J.-Q. Liang

item.title: [1★] Small-world networks yield tunable quantum codes at short circuit depth
item.author: Samuel Bevins, Gregory Bentsen
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Samuel Bevins, Gregory Bentsen

arXiv ID: 2611.31224 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Monitored random quantum circuits naturally generate quantum error-correcting codes. We generate quantum codes with tunable properties by implementing random Clifford circuits on Watts--Strogatz `small-world' networks and tailor code properties via three knobs: nonlocal graph rewiring, measurement rate, and circuit depth. On fully rewired networks, circuits of logarithmic depth produce codes with a finite rate and an extensive mean contiguous distance with failure probability substantially lower than codes produced from local circuits. These small-world codes form at a circuit depth growing as lnn\ln n compared to polynomial depths required for codes produced from local networks. Rewiring also moves the purification transition to higher measurement rates and changes its critical exponents. Connectivity is thus a knob for designing codes.

Samuel Bevins, Gregory Bentsen

item.title: [1★] Resilience of Entangling Gates to Spatiotemporally Correlated Noise
item.author: Xinru Tang, ..., Jelena Klinovaja, Daniel Loss
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Xinru Tang, ..., Jelena Klinovaja, Daniel Loss

arXiv ID: 2611.31114 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

As quantum processors scale, spatially and temporally correlated noise is emerging as a limiting factor in the fidelity of multiqubit gates. Here we show that this makes the choice of entangling operation a first-order design decision: for two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits, the CZ and √iSWAP\sqrt{\mathrm{iSWAP}} gates exhibit a pronounced resilience to correlated noise relative to the SWAP gate, even though correlated fluctuations of the entangling interaction can degrade gate performance to a level comparable to that of local noise. We trace this hierarchy to the redistribution of noise-sensitive channels away from zero frequency and show it to hold for noise spectra dominated by low-frequency weight, including 1/f1/f and Lorentzian. These results follow from a general expression, derived here, for the average gate infidelity under arbitrary spatiotemporal noise correlations, valid for generic multiqubit systems and system-environment coupling structures. The infidelity takes the form of a spectral overlap between the noise correlation matrix and a gate-dependent filter function, in which the coherent dynamics of the gate itself shapes the spectral window through which correlated fluctuations enter. The framework converts measured noise correlations into quantitative error budgets and provides a concrete design principle for selecting entangling operations in scalable quantum architectures.

Xinru Tang, ..., Jelena Klinovaja, Daniel Loss

item.title: [1★] Coherence transfer under bounded channel capacity
item.author: Dhruv Baheti, Karol Horodecki
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Dhruv Baheti, Karol Horodecki

arXiv ID: 2611.30680 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We investigate quantum coherence transfer between two parties whose local reference bases are misaligned, under a constraint on the capacity of the quantum communication channel. Within the resource theory of coherence, we formulate the task as maximizing the coherence received by Bob when Alice is restricted to Maximally Incoherent Operations (MIO) in her local basis. We first analyze two single-shot protocols, based on direct and locally entangled transmission, and derive their phase-optimized coherence yields. We further investigate their performance when Bob's reference basis is unknown, averaging over uniformly distributed basis configurations. In the asymptotic regime, we exploit the reversibility of coherence under MIO to characterize achievable transfer rates in terms of Alice's initial coherence. For single-qubit transmission, we derive an analytical lower bound using pure-state conversions and identify a regime in which the optimal yield saturates the channel capacity.

Dhruv Baheti, Karol Horodecki

item.title: [1★] Universal stabilizer correlations in chaotic eigenstates
item.author: Zhi-Han Liu, Hao-Yue Qi, Wei Zheng
item.content:encoded:

Authors: Zhi-Han Liu, Hao-Yue Qi, Wei Zheng

arXiv ID: 2611.30485 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Entanglement and nonstabilizerness provide complementary perspectives on quantum-state structure. In this work, we find that the stabilizer correlation, defined as the difference between the Rényi-22 mutual information and the mutual stabilizer Rényi entropy, approaches a universal constant for chaotic eigenstates. This constant is determined solely by the symmetries, and quantifies the correlation that does not contribute to nonstabilizerness. We identify this universal stabilizer correlation analytically via random-state ensembles, which give log27\log_2 7 (GOE) and log24\log_2 4(GUE) without extra symmetries, log214\log_2 14 and log28\log_2 8 under spin-inversion parity or half-filling magnetization. While imposing reflection or translation symmetry leaves these values unchanged. Exact calculations for a chaotic mixed-field Ising chain confirm the predicted plateau and finite-size approach. Integrable free-fermion and strongly disordered eigenstates behave qualitatively differently. This universal stabilizer correlation reveals a characteristic structure of chaotic eigenstates beyond entanglement or nonstabilizerness alone.

item.author: Kai Li, Masahito Ueda
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Kai Li, Masahito Ueda

arXiv ID: 2611.30441 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quasiparticles play a central role in understanding closed quantum many-body systems, as they reduce complex many-body problems to effective single-particle descriptions and connect directly to spectroscopic measurements. In open quantum systems, the interplay between coherent dynamics and dissipation gives rise to unique phenomena, such as the Liouvillian skin effect and strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking. This raises a fundamental question: how can the quasiparticle picture be extended to open quantum systems to account for such phenomena and enable the experimental probing of quasiparticle spectra? Here we introduce coherent and incoherent Liouvillian quasiparticles, defined by responses to perturbations acting on one side and both sides of the density matrix, respectively. We propose spectroscopy protocols that couple the system to auxiliary levels, either coherently or via a dissipative pulse, to measure the corresponding complex quasiparticle energies. Numerical simulations of Liouvillians with skin effects validate these protocols, revealing nontrivial spectral winding associated with unidirectional transport in real space. Notably, coherent and incoherent quasiparticles can propagate in opposite directions within the same system. Furthermore, in models exhibiting weak and strong-to-weak U(1)U(1) spontaneous symmetry breaking, our results unveil gapless Nambu-Goldstone modes in the coherent and incoherent quasiparticle spectra, respectively; the other quasiparticle spectrum remains gapped in each case. Our work provides a unified framework for theoretically describing and experimentally probing coherent and incoherent quasiparticles in open quantum many-body systems.

Abstract:

The unknown Hamiltonian has bounded, translation-invariant on-site and nearest-neighbour interactions on a 3D cubic lattice with local dimension three. The field coupling is known, and all models share a known boundary field penalizing one local level. The limiting order parameter is uniformly separated across the transition. Each query returns an independently prepared Gibbs or ground state at an adaptive field and system size. For error ϵ\epsilon and fixed confidence, we prove an exponential separation between two size caps at the same temperature. There are absolute constants 0<c0<C0<c_0<C and c1>0c_1>0 such that, at inverse temperature β=c1/ϵ\beta=c_1/\epsilon, restricting side lengths to L≤c0/ϵL\le c_0/\epsilon requires exp(Ω(1/ϵ))\exp(\Omega(1/\epsilon)) copies in worst-case expectation, even with collective measurements. Allowing L≤C/ϵL\le C/\epsilon permits O(log2(1/ϵ))O(\log^2(1/\epsilon)) copies and O(ϵ−3)O(\epsilon^{-3}) total spins, using local measurements and polynomial classical postprocessing. The minimax expected total spin count is Θ(ϵ−3)\Theta(\epsilon^{-3}) uniformly for β≥c1/ϵ\beta\ge c_1/\epsilon. At fixed positive temperature it is Θβ(ϵ−2)\Theta_\beta(\epsilon^{-2}), attained from one- and eight-site Gibbs states followed by exponential classical computation. For ground-state copies it is Θ(ϵ−3)\Theta(\epsilon^{-3}). The lower bound uses a three-state ferromagnet whose boundary suppresses the sector carrying transition information. Abstract:

We study the reconstruction and geometry of 4×44 \times 4 quantum Sudoku, viewed as arrays of rank-one projections whose rows, columns and blocks decompose the identity. We give necessary and sufficient conditions for two prescribed opposite blocks to admit a completion, prove its uniqueness, and obtain explicit reconstruction formulas, also expressed in the language of quantum logic. The sixteen overlaps between these blocks determine the unitary equivalence class of the grid, while the number of nonzero overlaps equals its cardinality. Using a matrix representation, we parametrise the equivalence classes by five closed squares, with the sides of one square identified with the diagonals of the other four. The quotient by classical cell symmetries is a closed disc containing exactly two classical classes. Finally, measurement in the basis of the first block gives a fractional Sudoku that retains the full unitary class and is a convex combination of at most four classical grids. This measurement map embeds the five-square model into a seven-dimensional polytope whose vertices are the twelve classical Sudoku.

Authors: Daniele Amato, ..., Giovanni Gramegna, Arturo Konderak

arXiv ID: 2611.28906 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Quantum channels provide the mathematical framework for describing the evolution of open quantum systems, i.e., quantum systems interacting with an environment. This review focuses on the long-time or asymptotic dynamics of open quantum systems, a topic of growing interest due to its relevance for quantum information theory and noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices. We present a comprehensive analysis of homogeneous evolutions in both discrete and continuous time, treating the dynamics in full generality within the Schrödinger and Heisenberg pictures. By systematically studying the spectral properties of quantum channels, we present general structure theorems that characterize asymptotic behaviour, illustrated through several paradigmatic examples. We further discuss how the asymptotic dynamics can be exploited for dissipative state engineering, the identification of decoherence-free subspaces, the design of quantum error-correction schemes, and the evaluation of the asymptotic capacities of quantum channels.

Authors: Bhuwan Joshi, ..., Zhi Xiang Chong, Liyi Li

arXiv ID: 2611.28388 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Hamiltonian simulation is a central application of quantum computing, yet most existing compilers offer no machine-checked guarantee that the circuits they produce approximate the intended evolution. The previous QBlue compiler verifies a Hamiltonian simulation compiler containing only Trotter-based algorithms. It takes a Hamiltonian written over Pauli strings, a simulation time, and an error bound, and produces a circuit or analog schedule that is proven, in the Rocq proof assistant, to approximate the ideal time evolution within that bound and proves a single end-to-end error bound that composes the errors of the individual stages; the compiler uses it to select, by resource estimation, the cheapest algorithm that meets the user's bound. This paper advances the verification efforts with two further steps. First, we extend QBlue to QBlueBE\textsf{QBlue}_{\texttt{BE}} by verifying another important compilation method for Hamiltonian simulation: block-encoding-based (BE-based) algorithms. Second, we empirically evaluate 279 Hamiltonian simulation programs against the state-of-the-art BE-based compiler, PennyLane. For many programs, our compiler shows a 94%94\% gate reduction compared to PennyLane. Additionally, we also discover issues and bugs in PennyLane. We also compare Trotter- and BE-based algorithms, providing a practical comparison for the long-standing debate over which algorithms perform better. Our results surprisingly show that Trotter-based algorithms may gain a practical advantage, even though BE algorithms have a theoretical advantage.

item.title: [1★] Bayesian Quantum Thermometry of Ultracold Gases with Non-Equilibrium Single-Atom Probes
item.author: Julian Feß, ..., Martí Perarnau-Llobet, Artur Widera
item.content:encoded:
Scites: 1 ★

Authors: Julian Feß, ..., Martí Perarnau-Llobet, Artur Widera

arXiv ID: 2611.27584 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Precise thermometry is essential for experiments with ultracold quantum gases, but conventional techniques such as time-of-flight thermometry are destructive and lose sensitivity at low atomic densities. Quantum probes provide an alternative route by encoding temperature information in accessible internal degrees of freedom. Here, we implement Bayesian thermometry with non-equilibrium spin-based single-atom probes immersed in an ultracold atomic bath. Temperature-dependent spin-exchange collisions map the bath temperature onto the internal spin populations of the probe atoms. Measurements of these populations are then used to iteratively update a Bayesian temperature estimate. We connect the information gained at different measurement settings to the underlying spin dynamics, identifying intersections of temperature-dependent population trajectories as a source of thermometric ambiguity. Using the expected information gain to optimize measurement settings, we experimentally compare unoptimized, a priori optimized, and adaptively optimized protocols. Both optimized protocols accelerate convergence, with the adaptive protocol reducing the average number of measurements required to reach a prescribed precision by a factor of 2.5 compared with the unoptimized protocol. In the many-measurement regime, we further characterize the protocols through their asymptotic error scaling and the accumulation of Fisher information, while testing consistency with the expected Cramér-Rao bound (ECRB) and the Bernstein-von Mises theorem. These results connect the microscopic dynamics of a quantum probe to efficient measurement design and establish Bayesian spin thermometry as a practical approach for ultracold-gas experiments.

item.content:encoded:

Authors: Pouriya Ghadimi, ..., Martin Eigel, Richard M. Milbradt

arXiv ID: 2611.27408 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Matrix product state time evolution relies on compression to control the growth of bond dimensions, but compression can break the conservation laws of the equation being solved. A truncation is not the flow of a Hermitian generator, so even a small truncation error can violate exact algebraic identities of the Schrödinger equation. For any matrix product state integrator that leaves the state in canonical form with an orthogonality center, a scalar correction restores an admissible global invariant after compression whenever the resulting scalar quadratic constraint equation admits a real root, without enlarging any bond dimension. Rank-preserving recovery searches other canonical centers when that correction fails. The geometry of the low-rank manifold provides sufficient conditions for conservation by the fixed-rank projected flow and bounds what corrections within a frozen center frame can achieve. Numerical experiments demonstrate that recovery can be required even along accurate truncated trajectories.

Abstract:

item.content:encoded:
Scites: 0 ★

Authors: Zhen-huan Yang, Dan-Bo Zhang

arXiv ID: 2611.30747 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

Autonomous quantum engines seek to convert energy supplied by environments into useful work, yet dephasing is usually regarded as detrimental noise. Here we show that local dephasing can instead power a quantum engine: by disrupting ferromagnetic correlations in an interacting spin-1/21/21/2 ensemble, it injects energy that can be transferred through an LC resonator to a passive load. Remarkably, without any external periodic driving, the coupled system can self-organize into a time-crystalline work cycle that delivers sustained, reproducible power. Within homogeneous mean-field dynamics, we identify two distinct routes to such operation. At weak spin--resonator coupling, the dissipative time crystal of the unloaded working medium survives loading and drives the receiver. At stronger coupling, resonator backaction can disrupt cyclic operation, whereas appropriate load damping restores a stable, self-consistent periodic cycle of the composite system. Finite-size spin-diffusion simulations further reveal rapidly increasing uninterrupted operating times with different size dependences in the two regimes. Our results demonstrate how an autonomous quantum engine can self-organize its collective dynamics through interactions and load feedback to harness environmental noise for sustained cyclic work output.

Authors: Pegah Mohammadipour, Xiantao Li

arXiv ID: 2611.30746 (arxiv.org | scirate)

Abstract:

We develop analytical and statistical methods to improve the energy estimate from the real-time quantum Krylov diagonalization under a fixed measurement budget. We first express the leading energy variance as a function of the number of shots assigned to each circuit setting, accounting for both the sensitivity of the energy to the measured moments and the correlations among outcomes recorded in the same shot.We use an initial batch of measurements to choose how to allocate the remaining shots. Under fixed-model regularity assumptions, the resulting generalized least-squares energy estimator attains the minimum leading mean-square error (MSE) coefficient within the prescribed allocation class, with the initial measurements included in the total shot budget. Furthermore, we use the same data to reconstruct the Hamiltonian and overlap moments jointly by fitting them to a common nonnegative spectral measure. For asymptotically Gaussian moment errors, we characterize precisely when this reconstruction lowers the leading energy MSE in the case where two linearly independent inequalities describe the feasible moment perturbations to first order. Numerical experiments on spin and Hubbard models show that learned allocation can improve Ritz energy estimates at fixed total shot cost. The experiments also illustrate that enforcing spectral consistency can further reduce the energy estimation error.

Abstract:

We investigate the geometric properties of concatenated quantum gates, focusing on the distinction between geometric and holonomic quantum computation. We show that, although individual gates may be purely geometric, their concatenation does not generally preserve this property, since the cyclic states of the composite operation can accumulate nontrivial dynamical phases over the course of the concatenated evolution. In contrast, we demonstrate that concatenations of arbitrary single-qubit holonomic gates remain holonomic, provided that the parallel-transport condition holds throughout the evolution and the computational subspace undergoes cyclic evolution. The preservation of geometric or holonomic character under concatenation is an important prerequisite for extending arguments underlying geometric protection from individual gates to complete quantum circuits.

Abstract:

The information bottleneck function gives a measure of optimal preservation of correlation between some random variable XXX and some side information YYY while compressing XXX into a new random variable WWW with bounded remaining correlation to XXX. As such, the information bottleneck has found many natural applications in machine learning, coding and video compression. The main objective in order to calculate the information bottleneck is to find the optimal representation on WWW. This could in principle be arbitrarily complicated, but fortunately it is known that the cardinality of WWW can be restricted as |W|≤|X|+1|{\cal W}|\leq|{\cal X}|+1 which makes the calculation possible for finite |X||{\cal X}|. Now, for many practical applications, e.g. in machine learning, XX represents a potentially very large data space, while YY is from a comparably small set of labels. This raises the question whether the known cardinality bound can be improved in such situations. We show that the information bottleneck function can always be approximated up to an error δ(ϵ,|Y|)\delta(\epsilon,|{\cal Y}|) with a cardinality |W|≤f(ϵ,|Y|)|{\cal W}| \leq f(\epsilon,|{\cal Y}|), for explicitly given functions δ\delta and ff of an approximation parameter ϵ>0\epsilon>0 and the cardinality of Y{\cal Y}. Finally, we generalize the known cardinality bounds to the case were some of the random variables represent quantum information.
